title: Small words that make Dutch sound natural
intro: Dutch speakers add small words like even, maar, eens, toch, nou and gewoon to almost every request. They hardly change the meaning, but they set the tone: friendly, polite, impatient or encouraging. You hear them all day at the school gate and at home.

notes.title: even: just for a moment
body: Even makes a request small and quick, like “just for a second”. It makes almost any request sound friendlier.
Ik ga even … means you're popping out to do something.

examples.en: I'm just going to take a quick shower.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 15: Modal particles
links.note: covers wel, even, eens and maar

notes.title: maar: go ahead
body: In a command, maar means “go ahead” or “just”. It gives permission or encouragement.
It can also sound like giving up: doe maar wat je wilt means “do whatever you want, then”.

examples.en: Never mind, I'll do it myself.

notes.title: eens: have a go, take a look
body: Eens makes a command lighter, like “have a go” or “take a look”. Kijk eens! means “Look!”. People often say it as ’s.
Eens even together means do it now, it won't take long.

examples.en: Read the text out loud for a moment.

notes.title: nou and toch: impatience
body: In a command, nou and toch show impatience, like “come on” or “already”. Use them with your own child, not with the teacher. This use of nou works in commands and questions, not in statements.
At the end of a question, toch asks for agreement: je komt toch ook? means “you're coming too, right?”

notes.title: gewoon: just, simply
body: Gewoon means normal. In a sentence it often means “just” or “simply”: the easy, obvious choice.

examples.nl: Je kunt [gewoon] naar de ingang lopen.
examples.en: You can just walk to the entrance.
Why don't we just make sandwiches?

notes.title: misschien and soms in questions
body: Misschien in a request makes it extra polite, like “could you maybe”.
Soms in a question means “by any chance”: weet je soms waar mijn sleutels zijn?

examples.en: Could you maybe wait a moment?

examples.nl: Weet je [soms] wie er gewonnen heeft?
examples.en: Do you happen to know who won?

cards.nl: Kun je me even helpen met deze doos?
cards.en: Can you help me with this box for a sec?

reply.nl: Ja hoor, waar moet hij heen?

cards.en: Can I ask something quickly?
cards.rule: even makes it polite and quick.

cards.en: I'm just going for a quick run.
cards.rule: Ik ga even …: popping out to do something.

cards.en: I'm just going to take a quick shower.
cards.rule: Ik ga even …: popping out to do something.

cards.en: Wait a second!
Come on in.

cards.nl: Probeer het maar, het is niet eng.
cards.en: Go on, try it, it's not scary.
Come and sit next to me.
Do whatever you want, then.

cards.nl: Laat maar, ik doe het zelf.
cards.en: Never mind, I'll do it myself.
Look at that car!
Have a taste, it's good.
Put your shoes on already!
Come on, we're late!

cards.nl: Stop nou toch eens met zeuren!
cards.en: Stop whining already!
cards.rule: nou toch eens: you've really had enough.

cards.en: You're coming too, right?
cards.rule: toch at the end: asking for agreement.

cards.nl: Ga toch maar gewoon naar bed, je bent moe.
cards.en: Just go to bed, you're tired.
cards.rule: toch maar gewoon: friendly but firm advice.

cards.nl: Je kunt gewoon naar de ingang lopen.
cards.en: You can just walk to the entrance.

cards.nl: Waarom maken we niet gewoon broodjes?
cards.en: Why don't we just make sandwiches?
Could you maybe wait a moment?
cards.rule: misschien even: extra polite and short.

cards.nl: Weet je soms wie er gewonnen heeft?
cards.en: Do you happen to know who won?
cards.rule: soms in a question: by any chance.
